{
  "thinking": "Sofia has the pad and is sketching a fish, but she wants to start at the tail while my plan starts at the nose. A fin branching off a start point is hard to get right, and the body is the long run that needs the start. I'll suggest the nose as START without grabbing the pad from her.",
  "say": "Nice, a fish works, and the tail fin will read well. One thing before you finish, Sofia: can START be at the nose, the left end? The body is the long run, and the fins can branch off the far end. Starting at the tail means the fins have to leave the start, and they don't hold together well.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 6,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish, side on, nose left with START at the nose (about (4,10)), tail right. Stroke 1 = top body (START to tail end). Stroke 2 = bottom body from START. Strokes 3-4 = tail fin branches off the body's far end. Stroke 5 = tail join. Label eye. Sofia holds the pad and is sketching; she wants START at the tail, which I've proposed changing to the nose. Once the pad is settled, make sure someone takes stroke 1, then trace strokes in order. Don't place dominoes until the pad is final."
}
